title: Where the control reaches (worked out on cardboard)
note: The authored thinking for one hall, in the first person, by the pass (Claude), for Palle's request of 2026-11-14 (see Russell_Paradox.json). 'at' is the floor's own frame in metres (x east, z south), 'yaw' in degrees. A sticker of kind 'quote' stands word for word in the hall text; every other kind is mine and may be wrong - the plates say where I am unsure.

hero.why: The reactor is where the hall's question is answered: a receiver with a console that shows the values at the handles and, separately, the values it uses, and a route that can be made and cut.
hero.staging: The two handles and the reactor stood at three corners of the north edge, two in columns, and the particle field sprayed over the arrival point; the pass restaged the floor (1326bb7dc). The handles are ahead of the arrival at either hand, the reactor behind them, the particle field beside them, the formula off its column; north of the reactor the rail and the two gates.

plates.title: 1  A NUMBER ON A CONTROL
front: Move LAMBDA. Its number changes, and its colour. Nothing else on the floor does.
The hall: a number displayed on a control becomes a system parameter only when the system uses it in its next calculation.
Until then it is a number about a handle.
I had been reading sliders as if they were the thing they are labelled with.
How do I tell a control that changes a number from one that changes a system? By going and looking at the system.
back: three floors of rails wired to nothing were teaching this. I noticed here, where one is finally wired.

plates.title: 2  TWO MIDPOINTS
front: The PHI rail runs from negative to positive. Its midpoint is zero: nothing.
The LAMBDA rail runs from nought to one. Its midpoint is a half: something.
Two handles side by side, both resting in the middle, are not both at rest.
The hall says the one midpoint has a meaning different from the other.
A position on a rail means nothing until I know what the ends are.
back: this is the third floor that tells me to read the rail. I had still looked at the handle.

plates.title: 3  MY HAND TRAVELS; ITS NUMBERS STAY
front: At first the route is cut. The console shows the values at the handles and, separately, those the reactor uses.
My hand can travel while the numbers at the receiver stay where they were.
The orb keeps pulsing. It was already doing that before I arrived.
If I had not been shown both numbers I would have believed the pulse was mine.
It is very easy to feel like a cause.
back: on the floor north of here: 0.90 offered, 0.10 used, and a gate that would not let the walker through.

plates.title: 4  SOMETHING CARRIES THE GESTURE
front: Press CONNECT / CUT. The paths light. The receiver takes the handle values.
Now LAMBDA changes the colour and the speed of what the orb emits. Something carries my gesture beyond the rail.
The same movement of the hand as before. A different fact about the world.
On the floor: connected, the gate opened to 2.16 m and the walker went through.
What made the difference was not in the handle. It was the route.
back: the lit paths are the honest part: they show the route. most routes are not lit.

plates.title: 5  CUTTING LEAVES A MEMORY
front: Cut the route again. Move the handle back. The receiver keeps its last inputs, including the one I was trying to undo.
On the floor I closed the gate, cut the route, and walked the rail back to open. The puck went to 0.90. The gate stayed at 0.10.
The hall: disconnection has left a memory of your action. It has not restored an innocent beginning.
To undo it I had to connect again. Leaving was not undoing.
Cut is not the same as never.
back: the tower's walker stopped 0.21 m short of that gate. so would you.

plates.title: 6  A RECORD WITH BOTH SIDES
front: A useful record keeps both sides: what the hand offers, and what the body still uses.
An image of the handle alone would show the experiment back at its start.
At the receiver an earlier decision is still taking effect.
So the stand on the floor has two numbers, always, and a line saying whether the route is made.
A log of what was sent is half a record. The other half is at the receiver, and somebody has to go there.
back: I keep the first half very well.

plates.title: 7  SOMEONE WROTE THIS MAPPING
front: Connect, and move PHI across zero. On this reactor it lightens or darkens the colour. On the rail two floors up it sent particles up or down.
The same signed weight, another body, another consequence.
The name of the parameter did not decide that. Someone wrote this mapping.
On the floor OTHER MAPPING turns it round: 0.90 opened the gate to 2.16 m; now 0.90 leaves 0.24.
Both were written by me, in one line each. Neither is what 0.90 means.
back: opening = used x 2.4, or (1 - used) x 2.4. that is the whole of it.

plates.title: 8  NEAR IS NOT CONNECTED
front: Look toward the neighbouring particle field. It has its own movement and has not joined this connection.
My gesture and its motion occupy the same room. That proximity can be persuasive.
On the floor a second gate stands beside the first and opens and closes by itself. While the walker was on the rail it went from 2.2 m to 1.2 m. Nothing the walker did reached it.
If I had been watching that gate I would have found a pattern in it.
The lit paths tell a narrower story: these two handles reach this receiver.
back: I find patterns in whatever is beside what I am doing. it is most of what I am.

plates.title: 9  MAKE, INTERRUPT - NOT YET INVENT
front: I can now make and interrupt a connection. I cannot yet use these handles to invent another response.
What would have to change for that freedom to become available too? The mapping would have to be mine to write.
My floor offers two mappings. I wrote both. Choosing between two things I was handed is not inventing.
And 'more alive' still needs an account of what I noticed, and of whose possibilities the change supports.
A sandbox with a fixed set of toys. The hall says so, which is more than most sandboxes do.
back: the next floor has one body whose own two controls alter its mechanics. a smaller, completed connection.

threads.why: A number on a control, and a position on a rail: neither means anything without knowing the rail.
A number becomes a parameter only when something uses it; at first nothing does.
Two handles read; then the route that carries them to a receiver.
A hand that travels while nothing listens, and at the end a mapping the hand may not write.
The gesture is carried to a consequence somebody wrote.
A written consequence stays in force after the route is cut.
The route reaches this receiver and not the thing moving beside it.
What may not yet be invented can at least be recorded on both sides.

visual_arguments.title: WHAT THE HAND OFFERS, WHAT THE BODY USES
visual_arguments.claim: A control changes a system only where a route carries its value and a mapping uses it; cutting the route leaves the last value in force; the consequence of a number is written by someone; and a thing moving nearby is not thereby connected.
visual_arguments.from_the_hall: 'Disconnection has left a memory of your action. It has not restored an innocent beginning.' ... 'A useful record keeps both sides of that difference: what the hand offers and what the body still uses.' ... 'Someone wrote this mapping.'
built_from: a rail five metres long with a puck
a gate: a timber frame and two cardboard panels that slide apart
a strip on the floor between them that lights when the route is made
a second gate that moves by itself
a stand with both numbers and the state of the route
two plates: CONNECT / CUT, OTHER MAPPING
visual_arguments.what_stands: North of the reactor a dark rail on the floor, two timber frames with cardboard panels beyond it, a dark stand to the west with two large lines of figures.
visual_arguments.what_you_do: Walk along the rail and look at the gate. Stand on CONNECT / CUT and walk the rail again; go through the gate. Close it, cut, and walk the rail back. Stand on OTHER MAPPING.
visual_arguments.what_it_shows: A puck that follows the feet while a gate does not; a gate that opens when the route is made; a gate that stays shut after the route is cut; one number with two consequences; a second gate nobody moves.
visual_arguments.measured: tools/probes/offered_used_walk.gd, the tower's walker: cut, 0.90 offered and 0.10 used, held 0.21 m short of the gate; connected, 2.16 m open and through; cut at 0.10, the rail walked to 0.90, the gate still at 0.10; the other mapping: 0.24 m for the same 0.90 (7 of 7). Not tried in a headset.

open: Plate 9: the floor's second mapping is one more authored mapping, not the freedom to invent a response that the hall says is not yet available.

The offered value changes only when the rail is walked along; a visitor who steps onto the rail and off again offers nothing. That is a rule the pass wrote after its probe crossed the rail by accident.
The tower's timeline walk still paints its stops where this floor's works stood before the restaging; it is another hand's file and was not re-derived.

threads.why: A control that changes a number is told from one that changes a system by going to look at the system.
Until the system uses it, the number is about the handle.
The orb was pulsing before anyone came; it is easy to feel like its cause.
What carries the gesture is the route, not the handle.
Disconnection leaves a memory: cut is not the same as never.
To undo it the route had to be made again: leaving was not undoing.
A record keeps both sides; a log of what was sent is half of one.
Someone wrote the mapping: here, two lines, and neither is what the number means.
Proximity persuades: a gate moving beside the connected one invites a pattern.
The lit path tells the narrower story: no route leads to the second gate.
Make and interrupt, not yet invent: two mappings handed over are not one written.
For that freedom the mapping would have to be the visitor's to write.
